1. Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3.  The present petition has been filed by the petitioners under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 seeking quashing of FIR No.0323/2017 dated 01.06.2023 registered under Sections 498A/406/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Ranhola, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement dated 07.07.2022 arrived at between the parties.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 23:27:10 4.
This petition is accompanied by the Settlement dated 07.07.2022 and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
5. Petitioner nos.1 to 5 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the Investigating Officer.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
6. Issue Notice.

sentences.text: Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
She confirms that she has no objection to the quashing of the said FIR.
8. Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 15.03.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement dated 07.07.2022 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.4.50,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.2,50,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no.2 vide DD No.577694 issued on Punjab National Bank, in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.

As per the settlement, the child namely Pragya is living with the respondent no.2 and the custody of the child shall remain with respondent no.2 and petitioner no.1 shall not have any visitation right.

In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr1, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr.2 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr.3, this Court is (2013) 4 SCC 58 (2012) 10 SCC 303 (2014) 6 SCC 466 This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 23:27:10 of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

9. Accordingly, the petition is allowed and FIR No.0323/2017 registered under Sections 498A/406/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.:
Ranhola, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom are quashed.

10. Needless to state that the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way, effect the rights of the children of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 namely Pragya vis-a-vis her parents,
as may be available under law, in any matter whatsoever.
11.
Accordingly, the present petition, alongwith the pending application, if any, stands disposed of.
SAURABH BANERJEE, J SEPTEMBER 19, 2023/akr
